seo.title: Floatboat Coworker — A Work Agent for Delegated Tasks
seo.description: Delegate a defined task to an AI Work Agent that can use approved files and tools, complete the work, and return a reviewable deliverable.

hero.title: Delegate a task. Get back finished work.
hero.description: Give the Floatboat Coworker a clear outcome, the relevant materials, and approval boundaries. It handles the task inside your Agent Workspace and returns a deliverable you can inspect, revise, or accept.

demo.title: Brief the work instead of steering every step
demo.description: The Coworker turns a bounded assignment into an execution plan, uses approved project resources, and comes back with the requested artifact.

features.title: A Work Agent owns the task between brief and delivery.
features.description: Coworker is the task-facing role inside Floatboat—not the workspace itself and not an open-ended chat companion.

items.question: What is a Work Agent?
items.answer: A Work Agent accepts a bounded assignment, uses the approved context and tools needed to complete it, and returns a concrete result. The task can end when the handoff is accepted.

items.question: How is Coworker different from the Agent Workspace?
items.answer: Coworker is the agent role you delegate a task to. The Agent Workspace is the persistent environment that provides files, tools, rules, history, and review controls for that work.

items.question: Can the Coworker act without my approval?
items.answer: Routine steps can run within the scope you provide. Sensitive or consequential actions should remain behind explicit approval boundaries that you can review.

items.question: What can the Coworker deliver?
items.answer: Depending on the task and enabled tools, it can return documents, research, organized files, drafts, code, or other editable artifacts supported by the workspace.

items.question: How do I write a task that an agent can finish?
items.answer: Name the deliverable, point to the source files, specify the required format, and define a stopping point. “Prepare a comparison table from these three proposals for my review” is easier to verify than “handle procurement.”

items.question: What should I check before accepting an agent deliverable?
items.answer: Inspect the editable artifact, trace important claims to the supplied sources, and review any changes or unresolved assumptions. A completed run does not establish that a document is accurate or ready to send.

finalCta.title: Hand the Work Agent a deliverable, not a prompt
finalCta.description: Provide the source files, expected output, and approval boundary; review the returned draft before it becomes final work.
